text: Shelf after shelf of Hall challenge tickets, kept, sorted and dated,
going back further than anyone in this house has been alive.
They are all for the same Hall. This family collects one thing.
The kitchen. A chalkboard by the door with today's date on it
and, under the date, a number: 4. Then a second number: 0.
Challengers down. Challengers with a Crest.
A ledger of every Keeper the Stone Hall has had, with dates.
The current entry has been open for twelve years and counting.
Somebody has written NOT LIKELY in the margin, in pencil, kindly.
A map of the workings, hand-copied, pinned up and annotated
in a dozen hands over a dozen years: where the plates are,
where the stones go, and one furious line reading THEY MOVE THEM.
